title: Invariant-based master equation applied to driven qutrit coupled to a bath and a leaky cavity
authors: Sagarika Basak, A. Javadi, D. Blume
abstract: We employ a generalized approach to the master equation for driven open $N$-level ($N>2$) quantum systems using Lewis-Riesenfeld invariants, which avoids the driving-strength restrictions inherent to conventional approaches. We show that the invariant-based master equation provides a unifying generalized framework, which reduces to the frequently employed laboratory-frame master equations and the less frequently employed rotating-frame master equation framework under appropriate simplifications. Extending the prototypical two-level system, we show that the inclusion of another state coupled to the ground state via reservoir-induced dephasing gives rise to qualitatively new dissipative behaviors that are, in general, not captured by standard approximations. We also apply the invariant-based master equation framework to a driven quantum dot coupled to a leaky cavity, demonstrating the framework's ability to capture relevant dissipative dynamics without additional assumptions. Our work paves the way for quantum-control applications in the presence of dissipation.
summary: This paper introduces an Invariant-based Master Equation framework to model the dynamics of driven, multi-level quantum systems like qutrits coupled to baths and cavities. It demonstrates that this new method provides a more general description than standard laboratory or rotating-frame approaches. By analyzing spectroscopic signatures, the authors show its ability to capture complex dissipative physics missed by conventional approximations.
main_problem: Developing a reliable theoretical model for externally driven quantum dynamics in open systems, overcoming fundamental issues with conventional master equation approaches.
main_result: The invariant-based master equation provides a unifying generalized framework that accurately captures dissipative dynamics in complex driven systems, yielding distinct predictions compared to standard laboratory or rotating-frame approximations.
method: The authors employ the Invariant-based Master Equation (IME) framework, utilizing Lewis-Riesenfeld invariants derived from the isolated system Hamiltonian to model time evolution in open quantum systems.
model_or_system: The study focuses on a driven qutrit ($N=3$ level system) coupled to an environment bath and potentially a leaky cavity. The dynamics are governed by a total Hamiltonian including time-dependent driving terms.
key_observables: Fluorescence spectrum $S_{12}(\omega)$, which is the Fourier transform of a first-order correlation function, used to diagnose dissipative behavior.
important_parameters: Driving strengths ($\Omega_p, \Omega_s$), detunings, and various decay/dephasing rates ($\Gamma_\perp, \Gamma_\parallel$).
main_assumptions: The framework generally uses the Born-Markov approximation; however, it is designed to handle regimes where conventional approximations fail.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the qutrit states and show spectral features (like modified Mollow triplets) resulting from different coupling regimes and driving strengths.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the IME framework as a generalization of standard master equations, applies it to a driven qutrit/cavity system, derives explicit forms for dissipation coefficients in various frames, and compares predictions using fluorescence spectra analysis.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the complex problem of non-Markovian or strongly driven open quantum systems by proposing a generalized theoretical tool (IME) that unifies several existing but limited master equation formalisms.
